With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

faq.q: What is County Line Glen Valley?
faq.a: A Fraser Valley board sub-area in the Township of Langley — rural acreage country of equestrian estates, hobby farms and multi-acre parcels. It is one of eleven Langley sub-areas in the SnapStats data, on the Township side of the combined Langley board community (SnapStats, September 2026)

faq.q: How active is the County Line Glen Valley market?
faq.a: Very thin in the published data: in September 2026 the sub-area recorded 0 detached active listings with 1 sold (sales ratio NA, as published — a sale against zero snapshot inventory, not a trend), and 0 Condos & Townhomes listings with 0 sold. Langley community context for the same month was 449 detached listings / 64 solds and 699 attached listings / 128 solds (SnapStats, September 2026)

faq.q: What is the median price in County Line Glen Valley?
faq.a: SnapStats does not publish a sub-area median — medians exist at community level only, and the Langley community medians for September 2026 were $1,345,000 detached and $611,000 for Condos & Townhomes. Those are community figures, not this sub-area's figures; the live feed's first page ran from $1,975,000 to $7,999,900, which is feed data, not a median (SnapStats, September 2026)

faq.q: Can a Glen Valley acreage have a second home or a suite?
faq.a: It depends on ALR status and Township zoning, parcel by parcel. On ALR land, the ALC frame allows one principal residence up to 500 m² plus at most one additional detached residence of 90 m² (parcels 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha), with a suite only inside the principal residence; under Township Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 a secondary suite is capped at 120 m² gross floor area, one per principal unit (~/workspace/area-research-2026-11/rules-gaps-2026-11-01.md, read 2026-11-01).
